//: The dev server forwards /api to the .NET API, exactly as nginx does in the
delivered stack. Two things follow, and both are the point.
The browser only ever talks to one origin, so there is no cross-origin
request and the API needs no CORS policy at all — nothing to configure, and
no permissive rule that could outlive development.
Development and production then differ in who forwards, not in what the
frontend calls: apiBaseUrl is '/api' in both. A bug caused by an absolute
address can no longer hide until the stack is assembled.
The target is the API's published port from infra/docker-compose.yml. It is
also where `dotnet run --project backend/src/PhotoAssistant.Api` listens, so
the same proxy serves both ways of running the backend.
